page.layout: Running head centred at top ("PARS PRIMA.") with page number 127 at top right. Two medallion engravings (coins) side by side below the head. Beneath them one column of running text in two paragraphs. No marginal notes and no text below the text block.

main_text.p: PHILIPPVS, Amintæ filius, apud Macedones impera-uit anno mundi 3603. ante Christum natum 359. In Athe-nienses primò bellum mouit: vicit: modestissimè victoria vsus est. deinde aduersus Illyricos mouit, multáque horum milia, ce-cidit. hinc Thessaliâ non prædæ cupiditate, sed quòd exercitui suo Thessalorum equitum robur adiungere gestiebat, improui-sus expugnat. Cùm Methonam vrbem oppugnaret, de muris sagitta iacta dextrum Regis Philippi oculum effodit: quo vul-nere nec segnior ad bellum, nec iracundior aduersus hostes factus est: adeò vt pacem deprecantibus dederit, mitisque ad-uersus victos fuerit. Tandem totius Græciæ Imperator factus, parabat bellum in Persas, cùm à Pausania occiditur, ob priua-tam iniuriam: creditum quoque est immissum ab Olympiade Alexandri matre fuisse, nec ipsum Alexandrum ignarum pa-ternæ cædis extitisse, cùm ipse vereretur ne hæres regni insti-tueretur frater natu minor, ex Cleopatra nouerca susceptus. Consulito Iustin.li.7. & 8.& Diod.de gestis Philippi. Imperauit Macedoniæ annos 25. vixit 47.

OLYMPIAS Regis Molossorum filia, vxor fuit supradicti[?] Philippi Macedoniæ Regis, & Alexandri mater. hæc dolens se ob adulteria repudiatam, prælatámque sibi Cleopatram, parauit necem viro, vnà cum filio regni æmulo, qui fratrem ex nouerca fusceptum, timebat. Videto Iustinum vt supra.

page.notes: The two engravings are coins. The left one shows a bearded laureate head in profile, with the legend PHILIP[?] MACED. REX. The right one shows a helmeted female head in profile, with the legend OLIMPIAS and PHIL. The legends were read from the image and are not part of the running text. Printed "Consulito" appears with a long-s form; transcribed as printed. The word "supradicti" has a ligature at "cti" that is hard to read and is marked [?]. The first paragraph's line-end hyphens ("impera-uit", "insti-tueretur") are kept as printed.
